title: Security in Christ
definition: Security in Christ is the believer's safety in the saving hand, finished work, and continuing intercession of Jesus.
summary: Security in Christ teaches that believers are kept by the power, promise, and intercession of Jesus.
christFocus: Jesus Christ holds His people, loses none of those given to Him, and secures them by His power.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Security is not confidence in the believer's grip on God but in Christ's faithful hold on His people. The Savior who saves also keeps, intercedes, shepherds, and will raise His own on the last day. This doctrine gives assurance without encouraging careless living.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because fear can make believers think salvation depends on the strength of their emotions or consistency. Security points them to Christ's finished work and continuing care. It also protects against a false assurance that ignores repentance and faith.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rest in Christ's keeping power while continuing to follow Him. Bring fears of falling away to His promises and intercession. Encourage assurance that produces humility, watchfulness, and gratitude.
